locator.section: 8.2 Product stability -- Charge competition in OE(+.) decompositions: Stevenson's Rule

evidence.curator_note: Eq 8.3 row 1, the 'or' branch (unlabeled arrow). Same C-O cleavage as 8.3a but the charge is RETAINED on the oxygen-bearing fragment giving OCH3+ (1%), with the odd electron migrating to the departing butyl radical .C4H9. Consistent with Stevenson's rule this minor channel is disfavoured because IE(.OCH3)=8.6 eV > IE(C4H9.)=8.0 eV. Book draws 0 arcs (summary equation); the homolytic C-O cleavage (one sigma electron of bond 4-5 to C4 giving the butyl radical, one to O5 pairing with the oxygen odd electron) is reconstructed for electron balance. NOTE: 'OCH3+' as drawn is the methoxy oxenium cation CH3-O(+) (valence-1 oxygen); RDKit renders this open-shell with two unpaired electrons (triplet), hence radical_electrons=2. The ion actually observed at m/z 31 is commonly the closed-shell H-rearranged CH2=OH(+), but the book's scheme depicts direct charge retention on the intact methoxy group with no H shift, which is what is encoded here.

Cross-linked MOD rule IMS_8_3_ind (equation 8.3, cleaves the C-O bond). MISMATCH: the rule emits both fragments as cations (C4H9(+) and CH3-O(+)), charge +2 on the RHS, and fuses this 1% OCH3+ retention branch with the 25% C4H9+ migration branch (8.3a) into one non-conserving step; dropped by the conservation guardrail. Does NOT match this substrate. See rule_mismatches.

Book prints '1%' relative abundance under OCH3+. observed_mz 31.0178 is the curator-computed electron-mass-corrected monoisotopic m/z of CH3O+; the page prints only the % abundance and the fragment IE (8.6 eV), no m/z.
